_note: The failing Job is the slow step: backoffLimit 1 means two attempts with a doubling backoff between them, so verify-job-failed-after-retries waits up to 3 minutes internally. The CronJob is scheduled for 03:00 and never fires during the run — the manual `oc create job --from=cronjob/...` is what exercises its template, which is also how you would test one for real. Native sidecars (an initContainer with restartPolicy: Always) need Kubernetes 1.29+; the test cluster is 1.35.

steps.run: envsubst < job-migrate.yaml | oc apply -f - && oc wait --for=condition=complete job/db-migrate --timeout=180s
oc get jobs && oc get pods -l job-name=db-migrate
envsubst < job-failing.yaml | oc apply -f - && oc wait --for=condition=failed job/db-migrate-broken --timeout=240s
envsubst < cronjob-report.yaml | oc apply -f - && oc get cronjob nightly-report
oc create job report-now --from=cronjob/nightly-report && oc wait --for=condition=complete job/report-now --timeout=180s
oc patch cronjob nightly-report -p '{"spec":{"suspend":true}}' --type=merge && oc get cronjob nightly-report
envsubst < deployment-with-helpers.yaml | oc apply -f - && oc rollout status deploy/hello-dcs --timeout=240s
pod=$(oc get pod -l app=hello-dcs -o name | head -1); oc logs $pod -c setup; oc logs $pod -c heartbeat --tail=3
pod=$(oc get pod -l app=hello-dcs -o name | head -1); oc exec $pod -c hello-dcs -- cat /work/setup.txt; oc exec $pod -c hello-dcs -- tail -2 /work/heartbeat.log
